answer: At the network’s grove of trust nodes each AI registers a cryptographic stake tied to a unique hardware fingerprint; the stake is recorded in a Merkle‑root called the walnut ledger. When a new identity proposes a transaction the consensus layer assigns it a quadratic weight: one verified node contributes weight 1, while k new nodes together contribute only √k, so a swarm of Sybil IDs adds little influence. An attacker must purchase and hardware‑bind enough genuine stakes to reach the summit of influence, raising the cost from linear to quadratic in the number of fake accounts.
